modules.title: Foundations
modules.description: Evolution of money, TradFi/CeFi/DeFi, blockchain infrastructure, and smart contracts

questions.question: What core insight does the Yap Rai stone system illustrate about money?

options.text: Money must be portable to function
Money is a ledger technology — ownership can be agreed upon without moving the physical token
Only gold can serve as reliable money
Oral tradition cannot record value

questions.explanation: The Rai system separated possession from ownership through community consensus — conceptually similar to distributed ledger entries on a blockchain.

questions.question: What is the key difference between CeFi and DeFi?

options.text: CeFi uses crypto; DeFi does not
DeFi relies on smart contracts and protocols instead of centralized intermediaries holding custody
CeFi is always safer than DeFi
There is no practical difference

questions.explanation: DeFi replaces many intermediary functions with transparent, on-chain smart contract logic. CeFi still relies on trusted centralized entities.

questions.question: What problem does the blockchain trilemma describe?

options.text: The tradeoff between decentralization, security, and scalability
The difficulty of mining Bitcoin
Why stablecoins always depeg
How to avoid paying gas fees

questions.explanation: Blockchains typically optimize for two of decentralization, security, and scalability — improving one often constrains another.

questions.question: What is a smart contract?

options.text: A legal agreement between two lawyers
Self-executing code on a blockchain that runs when predefined conditions are met
A hardware wallet
A type of stablecoin

questions.explanation: Smart contracts automate agreements through code deployed on-chain, enabling DeFi primitives like swaps and lending without manual intermediaries.

questions.question: What does ERC-20 standardize on Ethereum?

options.text: NFT metadata only
Fungible token interfaces so wallets and exchanges can interact consistently
Proof-of-stake consensus
Layer 2 bridging

questions.explanation: ERC-20 defines a common interface for fungible tokens, enabling interoperability across DeFi applications.

modules.title: Access and Security
modules.description: Wallets, self-custody, security fundamentals, DEXs, and lending protocols

questions.question: What does 'not your keys, not your coins' mean?

options.text: Coins on an exchange in your account are fully under your self-custody
If you do not control the private keys, you rely on a third party to honor withdrawals
Hardware wallets are unnecessary
Private keys should be shared with support staff

questions.explanation: Custodial platforms control the keys backing your balance. Self-custody means you alone control access via your private keys.

questions.question: What is a common seed phrase security practice?

options.text: Store it in a cloud note for convenience
Never share it and store offline backups in secure locations
Email it to yourself encrypted with a weak password
Post it on social media for recovery help

questions.explanation: Seed phrases grant full wallet access. Offline, private storage is essential — anyone with the phrase controls the funds.

questions.question: How does an AMM DEX typically price trades?

options.text: Through an order book of bids and asks only
Using a mathematical formula based on token ratios in a liquidity pool
By random assignment
By government regulation

questions.explanation: Automated Market Makers use pool reserves and formulas (e.g. x*y=k) to determine prices without traditional order books.

questions.question: In DeFi lending, what happens when collateral value falls too far?

options.text: Nothing — loans are never closed automatically
The protocol may liquidate collateral to repay lenders
The borrower receives a bonus
Interest rates go to zero

questions.explanation: Liquidation mechanisms protect lenders by selling collateral when health factors breach protocol thresholds.

questions.question: What is a phishing attack in crypto?

options.text: Mining with renewable energy
Tricking users into signing malicious transactions or revealing secrets via fake sites or messages
A type of stablecoin arbitrage
Providing liquidity to a pool

questions.explanation: Phishing exploits human trust — fake interfaces and approvals can drain wallets without breaking cryptography.

modules.title: Advanced Concepts
modules.description: Stablecoins, flash loans, risk management, and Layer 2 scaling

questions.question: What is a primary risk of algorithmic stablecoins?

options.text: They always maintain peg through government guarantee
Death spirals when market confidence collapses and arbitrage mechanisms fail
They cannot be traded on DEXs
They have no smart contract code

questions.explanation: Algorithmic designs depend on incentives and confidence. Loss of peg can trigger reflexive selling and collapse.

questions.question: What makes flash loans unique?

options.text: They require no collateral and must be repaid within the same transaction block
They are only available to banks
They never charge fees
They lock funds for one year

questions.explanation: Flash loans are uncollateralized but atomic — if repayment fails, the entire transaction reverts.

questions.question: What is impermanent loss primarily associated with?

options.text: Hardware wallet failures
Providing liquidity to AMM pools when asset prices diverge
Staking ETH on Layer 1 only
Paying gas in stablecoins

questions.explanation: LPs may end up with a different asset mix vs. holding, especially when prices move sharply — fees may or may not compensate.

questions.question: Why do Layer 2 networks exist?

options.text: To eliminate the need for Ethereum entirely
To increase throughput and reduce fees while inheriting L1 security assumptions
To replace private keys with passwords
To ban DeFi applications

questions.explanation: Layer 2s batch transactions off mainnet, improving cost and speed while anchoring to Ethereum for security.

questions.question: What is a sensible risk management principle in DeFi?

options.text: Use maximum leverage on every trade
Size positions so a single loss cannot impair your entire portfolio
Ignore smart contract audits
Approve unlimited token allowances to every site

questions.explanation: Position sizing and diversification limit tail risk — a core framework taught throughout the course.
